name: AIR
what_it_holds: Jupyter-notebook scraper ('Airdna webscraper.ipynb') for active Airbnb/VRBO listings on AirDNA's public market pages, defaulted to El Paso, TX but configurable to other markets; includes a committed sample output file ep_str_data (1).xlsx. 2 commits, no license.
why_useful: A working method to pull AirDNA market-level STR listing/occupancy-style data for any US city on demand — directly targets gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from AirDNA-class sources), including Nevada/Florida/Texas/Hawaii/California/NYC markets if repointed. Catalogued as method only; not run per rules on scraping non-Airbnb sites needing a human ToS call.
geography: El Paso TX default, configurable to any AirDNA market
time_coverage: snapshot/current at run time, not historical
last_activity: unknown (2 commits, exact date not surfaced)
themes: State and city hotel occupancy and lodging-tax datasets (Nevada, Florida tourist development tax, Texas hotel occupancy tax, California TOT, NYC hotel occupancy tax, Hawaii TAT)
why_all: A working method to pull AirDNA market-level STR listing/occupancy-style data for any US city on demand — directly targets gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from AirDNA-class sources), including Nevada/Florida/Texas/Hawaii/California/NYC markets if repointed. name: layoffs-tracker
what_it_holds: DuckDB (layoffs.duckdb) + Streamlit dashboard built by ingesting the layoffs.fyi dataset via Kaggle API (ingest.py). 2,412 layoff events, 1,713 companies, 49 countries, 2020-2025. Weekly refresh via GitHub Actions, so re-pulling gives a point-in-time-ish snapshot each week even though layoffs.fyi itself is not versioned upstream. Airbnb had multiple disclosed layoff rounds (2020, 2023) that would appear as rows if still in the source.
why_useful: Headcount-proxy signal for gap #14/#15 (Airbnb hiring/layoffs as headcount proxy, corporate-structure signals) with a working, re-runnable pull script rather than a static file; weekly GH Actions refresh gives a crude vintage trail going forward from whenever this repo is queried.
themes: Airbnb corporate footprint signals: careers/Greenhouse job-posting scrapers, LinkedIn headcount trackers, layoffs.fyi data, Glassdoor/Indeed review datasets, GitHub org activity (GH Archive)
why_all: Headcount-proxy signal for gap #14/#15 (Airbnb hiring/layoffs as headcount proxy, corporate-structure signals) with a working, re-runnable pull script rather than a static file; weekly GH Actions refresh gives a crude vintage trail going forward from whenever this repo is queried.

A committed, queryable (DuckDB) mirror of the canonical layoffs.fyi tech-layoffs tracker — the actual source most 'layoffs data' searches point back to. Should contain Airbnb's 2020 layoff event (company, date, count, % of workforce) as one row, giving a directly comparable cross-company layoff-severity metric.

name: Global-Layoffs-Data-Cleaning-Project

name: Layoff-Insights-Unveiling-Trends-and-Opportunities-in-the-Tech-Industry
what_it_holds: Combines Layoffs.fyi data with WARN Act (Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification) layoff filings to analyze trends/causes/effects by industry and company type.
why_useful: WARN Act filings are a distinct, legally-mandated US federal/state data source for company-level layoff notices (separate from the layoffs.fyi crowd-sourced tracker) — a genuinely different headcount data lineage worth a human's follow-up, since state WARN databases are public and could show Airbnb-specific filings if any occurred.

name: layoffs-tracker (kadoa)
what_it_holds: Open-source dataset + interactive dashboard (Vite/React/sql.js) of ~42,000 mass-layoff and plant-closure notices aggregated from 45 state labor departments, normalized via kadoa.com's parsing pipeline. Ships a lazily-loaded full SQLite database plus a JSON summary file for the overview. MIT licensed, 137 commits.
why_useful: A second, independently-sourced/normalized WARN-notice dataset (different coverage/parsing than APVentureEngine's) — cross-checking two independent WARN aggregations reduces normalization risk before trusting any Airbnb-specific layoff date/count pulled from either.
